newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open slightly down after Dow dip.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open slightly down after Dow dip.

text.p: Australian stocks got off to a tentative start on Wednesday after the previous day's record close as dealers awaited more forceful moves after an announcement on the fate of nickel producer QNI Ltd.
"Everything is drifting at the moment," Reynolds & Co dealer Peter Struk said.
The All Ordinaries Index was down 2.3 points to 2679.4 at 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT) in light trade, while the June share index futures contract was 4.0 points at 2683.0.
A dip on Wall Street and the fall in the June share price index also contributed to the soft opening, Struk said.

Resources drove the All Ordinaries index to a record closing high on Monday and BHP, Australia's biggest listed company, was again among the most active stocks with a parcel of 1.5 million shares traded shortly after the opening.

Struk said the market was awaiting the outcome of a QNI board meeting, with an announcement expected on a possible takeover or major shareholding in Australia's second largest nickel producer by South African mining house Gencor Ltd.
"The interesting news is whether it will be a merger or a takeover," Struk said. "If it's a takeover, things will be bullish because funds will be redirected to other resources."
The solid trade in BHP bolstered the market while the banking sector was slightly down on apparent profit-taking, market watchers said.
